messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] declaring data as "int" or "real"
parts:
> On Wed, Oct 3, 2012 at 10:22 AM, Lucas Leemann <llee...@gmail.com <mailto:llee...@gmail.com>> wrote:
> I have a lot of binary explanatory variables. Does it matter whether I declare them as "int" or "real" with respect
> to runtime?

On 10/3/12 10:24 AM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> int is, overall, the best option and should be a little bit faster.
> That said, it won't be a big difference unless your
> model is very small and very simple.

The last sentence is key -- you should do whatever's
natural for the data, which for binary variables, would
be int.

If they're parameters (unknown), they need to be real.

If they're not parameters, what's fastest will depend
on what you do with them. One issue is that int is
32-bit and real is 64-bit, and smaller is usually faster.
So if you have an array of values and traverse them,
there's less memory paging for 32-bit values.
But if you have to take those ints which are not known
at compile time and convert them to doubles, that's
slower (but not nearly as slow as the reverse conversion
with floor(), round(), etc., or even a cast in C++), it
can be faster to just have them all be doubles.

- Bob
